title: Yellow Enel
summary: A Life-control deck. You keep adding cards to your Life, play Characters that come out for free when they're revealed as [Trigger]s, and the Leader saves you once a turn when your Life hits 0. Games are long, and you win them late.
gamePlan: Early turns: Streusen finds Big Mom Pirates cards, and Charlotte Pudding draws 3 if you trash a [Trigger] card.
Many of your Characters (Charlotte Daifuku, Charlotte Oven) have [Trigger] Play this card. When your opponent hits your Life and reveals one, it hits the table for free.
Use Zeus to K.O. a Character by taking a Life card into your hand. Then refill Life with Borsalino, Sweet 3 Generals or Marshall.D.Teach.
Late game: the 10-cost Charlotte Linlin turns all your 4000-power [Trigger] Characters into 8000 power on your turn. Swing with all of them.
Your Leader is your safety net: on your opponent's turn, when your Life becomes 0, you put the top card of your deck back into Life. That buys you one more turn, once per turn.

keyCards.why: Leader. Once per opponent's turn, refills 1 Life when you hit 0.
Charlotte Pudding. Trash a [Trigger] card to draw 3.
Zeus. 2 cost K.O. for a 5-cost-or-less Character, paid with a Life card.
Borsalino. [Blocker] that adds a Life card when you're at 2 or less.
Sweet 3 Generals. Draws, adds Life, and shrinks two Characters by 3000.
Charlotte Linlin. Makes your 4000-power [Trigger] Characters 8000 power on your turn.
0-cost Counter for +3000. As a [Trigger] it can refill your Life at 0.

howItWins: You survive longer than your opponent. Life keeps coming back, [Trigger]s give you free Characters, and Charlotte Linlin turns your small Characters into a big final attack.
weakTo: Decks that win with one huge turn of many attacks, since you can only refill once per turn.
Effects that negate [Trigger]s or trash Life cards.
Running out of deck: adding Life uses up deck cards, so watch your deck size in long games.
mulliganTips: Keep Streusen or Pudding and at least two Counter cards. You don't need big Characters early.
